white-forest.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Elzette into Diabell, Queen

One Elzette becomes two big monsters that protect each other. Elzette finds Silvy, Silvy finds the Field Spell Witch of the White Forest, and Witch finds a second Level 2. Silvy + that Level 2 make the Synchro Rciela, and Rciela + Elzette make the Level 8 boss Diabell. Diabellze and Diabellstar Vengeance join from the Diabell side, so the line ends on three Level 8s.

Starting hand: Elzette of the White Forest, Pressured Planet Wraitsoth · Normal Summon: Silvy of the White Forest

  1. Send Pressured Planet Wraitsoth from your hand to the GY to Special Summon Elzette. Elzette adds Silvy from your Deck.
  2. Normal Summon Silvy. She adds Witch of the White Forest (a White Forest Spell) from your Deck.
  3. Activate Witch of the White Forest. It adds Elzette, Azamina from your Deck. For the rest of the turn you can't Special Summon DARK monsters from the Extra Deck.
  4. Reveal Elzette, Azamina to Special Summon a White Forest monster from your hand. It can choose itself.
  5. Synchro Summon Rciela (Level 6) using Silvy (Level 4 Tuner) + Elzette, Azamina (Level 2). Azamina, sent as Synchro Material, adds Sinful Spoils of Subversion - Snake-Eye.
  6. Rciela was Special Summoned: send Witch of the White Forest from the field to the GY and add Diabellze (it counts as a White Forest card).
  7. Diabellze: send Snake-Eye from your hand to Special Summon itself. Its Summon effect sends Curse of Diabell from your Deck to the GY.
  8. Curse of Diabell was sent from the Deck, so it adds Filia Diabell (a Diabell Spell) to your hand.
  9. Synchro Summon Diabell, Queen (Level 8) using Rciela (Level 6 Tuner Synchro) + Elzette (Level 2). Because a Tuner Synchro was used, Diabell adds Witch of the White Forest back from your GY.
  10. Activate Filia Diabell to add Diabellstar Vengeance (a Level 8 Diabell monster) from your Deck.
  11. Diabellstar Vengeance: banish Filia Diabell (Spell) and Curse of Diabell (Trap) from your GY to Special Summon it. Filia was banished, so your Diabell monsters gain 500 ATK.

End board: Diabell, Queen + Diabellze + Diabellstar Vengeance, with Witch in hand. With 2+ Diabell monsters, Diabellze stops your opponent's effects destroying your monsters. When they activate something, Diabell can send Witch from your hand to Summon Rciela from the GY. That also returns Elzette from your GY to your hand. Vengeance (pay half your LP) destroys 1 of their cards.

  • Witch's search locks you out of DARK Extra Deck monsters (S:P Little Knight, Chaos Angel, Garura, Starving Venom, TY-PHON) for that turn.
  • Each White Forest card's effects are once per turn by name. A second Elzette can't use its Summon effect this turn.
  • If Silvy's search is stopped by Ash Blossom, still make Rciela and use Rciela's search to get Witch of the White Forest.
Line B — Diabellstar into Vengeance

This is the line when you don't open Elzette. WANTED finds Diabellstar, and Diabellstar Summons itself by sending 1 card. Diabellze then puts Diabellstar Vengeance in the GY, and Vengeance Summons itself back out. You end with three Diabell monsters that protect each other. Vengeance can destroy a card on your opponent's turn and then Summon a Synchro Tuner.

Starting hand: WANTED: Seeker of Sinful Spoils, Diabellze the White Witch, Pressured Planet Wraitsoth · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate WANTED: Seeker of Sinful Spoils to add Diabellstar the Black Witch from your Deck.
  2. Special Summon Diabellstar by sending Pressured Planet Wraitsoth from your hand to the GY.
  3. Diabellstar was Summoned: Set Sinful Spoils of Slumber - Morrian from your Deck.
  4. Diabellze: send the Set Morrian (a Trap) from your field to the GY to Special Summon Diabellze from your hand.
  5. Diabellze was Summoned: send Diabellstar Vengeance from your Deck to the GY. Vengeance always counts as a Sinful Spoils card.
  6. Diabellstar Vengeance: banish Pressured Planet Wraitsoth (Spell) and Morrian (Trap) from your GY to Special Summon it from the GY.
  7. WANTED in the GY: banish it to put the banished Morrian on the bottom of your Deck and draw 1 card.

End board: Diabellstar the Black Witch + Diabellze + Diabellstar Vengeance. Diabellze stops your opponent's effects destroying your monsters. On their turn, Vengeance (pay half your LP) destroys 1 of their cards. With another Diabell on the field, it then Summons Rciela, Silvera or Poplar from your Extra Deck.

  • You can Special Summon Diabellstar with its own effect only once per turn.
  • If Diabellze's send is negated, Vengeance never reaches the GY and you end on two monsters.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell. You discard 1 card and Fusion Summon using monsters from EITHER field, and nobody can respond to it. Going second, you use it to turn two of your opponent's best monsters, or one of theirs and one of yours, into one Fusion Monster on your side. Pick the Fusion from what the two monsters have in common. Your own pairs: Elzette + Silvy (both LIGHT Spellcasters) for Garura, and Elzette + Diabellze (LIGHT, different Types) for Mudragon.

Starting hand: Super Polymerization · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Super Polymerization by discarding 1 card. Neither player can respond to it.
  2. Both monsters share a Type and an Attribute but have different names → Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. If Garura later goes to the GY, you draw 1.
  3. Same Attribute but different Types → Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target it, or your monsters of its Attribute, with effects.
  4. Both are DARK monsters on the field (not Tokens) → Starving Venom Fusion Dragon.
  5. Same Type but different Attributes → Favorite HERO Flame Wingman.
  6. Their two monsters leave the field as Fusion Material, so destruction protection doesn't save them. Then attack.

End board: Their two key monsters are gone and you have a Fusion Monster to attack with. You can also Set Super Polymerization and use it on your opponent's turn.

  • You choose the Fusion Monster. Check the Type and Attribute shown on each card before you activate it.
  • Fusions that must be Summoned another way ("cannot be Fusion Summoned" or contact Fusions) are not legal choices.
  • Witch of the White Forest's DARK lock blocks Garura and Starving Venom. Use Super Polymerization before you activate Witch.
white-forest.str:
• Two self-sufficient engines.
  • Many Quick-Effect Synchros (Poplar, Diabell Queen).
  • Placement removal (Subversion, Vengeance Dragon, Doomed Dragon).
white-forest.weak:
• Field Zone congestion.
  • Witch's DARK lock cuts five Extra Deck options.
  • Elzette Azamina's Fusion effect dead.

Line A — Imsety into the Horus board

Imsety pays for itself. Send it and 1 other card from your hand to find King's Sarcophagus and draw. Once Sarcophagus is on the field, Horus monsters in your GY can Special Summon themselves. Sarcophagus also lets you send Hapi from your Deck to the GY, so both Level 8s come straight back out. They are hard to remove: effects that destroy without targeting can't touch them.

Starting hand: Imsety, Glory of Horus, Imsety, Glory of Horus · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Imsety: send it and your second Imsety from hand to the GY. Add King's Sarcophagus from your Deck, then draw 1.
  2. Activate King's Sarcophagus (a Continuous Spell).
  3. King's Sarcophagus: send the card you drew from your hand to the GY. Then send Hapi from your Deck to the GY.
  4. You control King's Sarcophagus, so Special Summon Imsety from your GY.
  5. Special Summon Hapi from your GY the same way.

End board: Imsety + Hapi + King's Sarcophagus. Non-targeting destruction can't hit Horus monsters. If an opponent's effect makes another card of yours leave the field, Imsety sends 1 card on the field to the GY. Hapi then adds or shuffles 2 cards from the GYs or banishment. Sarcophagus can also send a monster Imsety battles to the GY.

  • Imsety and Hapi each Special Summon from the GY only once per turn by name.
  • King's Sarcophagus's send effect works up to 4 times per turn. Each use costs 1 card from your hand.
  • Walls of the Imperial Tomb becomes "King's Sarcophagus" in the Field Zone, so it also turns on the GY Summons.
Line B — Mitsurugi Ritual into Murakumo

Mitsurugi Prayers finds the Ritual boss Ame no Murakumo, and Mitsurugi Ritual Summons it by Tributing two Level 4s straight from your Deck. Murakumo destroys every monster your opponent controls when it is Special Summoned. The Tributed Level 4s each search, which sets up a second Ritual for Futsu. Your opponent then faces a Quick Effect that says discard a card or your effect is negated.

Starting hand: Mitsurugi Prayers, Mitsurugi Ritual · Normal Summon: Mitsurugi no Mikoto, Kusanagi

  1. Activate Mitsurugi Prayers without Tributing: add Ame no Murakumo no Mitsurugi from your Deck.
  2. Activate Mitsurugi Ritual (hand mode). Ritual Summon Murakumo from your hand by Tributing Aramasa + Saji (4 + 4 = 8) from your Deck.
  3. Murakumo was Special Summoned: destroy all monsters your opponent controls. This matters when you go second.
  4. Aramasa was Tributed: it adds Futsu no Mitama. Saji was Tributed: it adds Mitsurugi Mirror.
  5. Activate Mitsurugi Mirror: Ritual Summon Futsu from your hand by Tributing Murakumo (Level 8) from your field.
  6. Murakumo was Tributed: it adds Kusanagi, then Special Summons itself. Its destroy-all effect was already used this turn.
  7. Normal Summon Kusanagi: add Saji back from your GY to your hand.

End board: Murakumo + Futsu + Kusanagi, with Saji in hand. When your opponent activates a card or effect, Murakumo makes them discard 1 card or the effect is negated. When they Special Summon, Futsu revives a Reptile from your GY. If another Reptile would be destroyed, Kusanagi can be Tributed instead, and that Tribute recovers a Mitsurugi card.

  • Mitsurugi Ritual's hand mode can Tribute from your Deck. The other mode Summons the Ritual Monster from your Deck instead, Tributing from hand or field. Each mode is once per turn.
  • You can only activate 1 Mitsurugi Prayers per turn.
  • Each Murakumo effect is once per turn, so its revival in step 6 does not destroy the board a second time.
Line C — Rank 8 into Pain Gainer (going second)

When you go second and Line A leaves you Imsety + Hapi, you can turn them into removal. They are two Level 8s, so they make Number 97: Draglubion. A DARK Rank 8 with 2 materials can become Number 84: Pain Gainer. Pain Gainer destroys every face-up monster your opponent controls whose DEF is at or below its own.

Starting hand: Imsety, Glory of Horus, Imsety, Glory of Horus · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Build Imsety + Hapi with King's Sarcophagus (Line A, steps 1–5).
  2. Xyz Summon Number 97: Draglubion (Rank 8) using Imsety + Hapi. Your opponent can't target it.
  3. Xyz Summon Number 84: Pain Gainer on top of Draglubion (a DARK Rank 8 with 2 materials). The materials move over.
  4. Pain Gainer's DEF becomes 2200 (Rank 11 × 200). Detach 1 material: destroy each face-up opponent's monster with 2200 or less DEF.
  5. While it has material, your opponent takes 600 damage each time they activate a Spell or Trap.

End board: Number 84: Pain Gainer with 1 material and a cleared field. Going first, keep Imsety + Hapi instead. Xyz Summoning gives up King's Sarcophagus's protection.

kashtira-maliss.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Dormouse into Red Ransom

Maliss monsters come back when they are banished: pay 300 LP and they Special Summon themselves. So you banish your own cards on purpose. Dormouse banishes White Rabbit from the Deck, White Rabbit returns and Sets a Maliss Trap, and Haggard Lizardose recycles Dormouse into the Link-3 Red Ransom. Red Ransom finds the Field Spell, and the Field Spell banishes one more Maliss to bring it out too.

Starting hand: Maliss <P> Dormouse · Normal Summon: Maliss <P> Dormouse

  1. Normal Summon Dormouse. Its Main Phase effect banishes White Rabbit from your Deck, and your Maliss monsters gain 600 ATK this turn.
  2. White Rabbit was banished: pay 300 LP to Special Summon it. From now on you can only Special Summon Link Monsters from the Extra Deck this turn.
  3. White Rabbit was Summoned: Set Maliss <C> MTP-07 from your Deck.
  4. Link Summon Haggard Lizardose (2 monsters with different names) using Dormouse + White Rabbit.
  5. Lizardose: banish Dormouse (900 ATK) from your GY and target Lizardose. Dormouse was banished, so pay 300 LP to Special Summon it.
  6. Link Summon Maliss <Q> Red Ransom (2+ monsters including a Maliss) using Lizardose + Dormouse.
  7. Red Ransom was Special Summoned: add Maliss in Underground (a Maliss Spell) from your Deck.
  8. Activate Maliss in Underground: banish Chessy Cat from your Deck. Chessy Cat was banished, so pay 300 LP to Special Summon it.

End board: Red Ransom + Chessy Cat + Maliss in Underground + a Set MTP-07. While Red Ransom points to a monster, the original ATK and DEF of your opponent's Effect Monsters are switched. While you control a Maliss Link, Underground lets them attack only your Maliss Links. On their turn, MTP-07 adds a Maliss monster and banishes 1 card on the field.

  • Every banish-and-return costs 300 LP and locks you to Link Monsters from the Extra Deck for the turn.
  • Each Maliss card's effects are once per turn by name.
  • Don't resolve Kashtiratheosis first: it locks you to Xyz Monsters, which shuts off every Maliss Link.
Line B — Kashtira on an empty field (going second)

The Kashtira monsters only Special Summon themselves while you control no monsters, so they come first, before any Maliss plays. Fenrir drops onto an empty field. Kashtiratheosis turns it into a second body by pulling Unicorn from the Deck. Fenrir banishes 1 of your opponent's face-up cards face-down when it attacks, and Unicorn banishes a card from their Extra Deck when they use a monster effect.

Starting hand: Kashtira Fenrir, Kashtiratheosis · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. You control no monsters: Special Summon Kashtira Fenrir from your hand.
  2. Activate Kashtiratheosis targeting Fenrir (EARTH). Special Summon Kashtira Unicorn (WIND) from your Deck in Defense Position. Then you can only Special Summon Xyz Monsters from the Extra Deck this turn.
  3. Fenrir's Main Phase effect: add your second Kashtira Fenrir from the Deck for next turn.
  4. Fenrir declares an attack: banish 1 face-up card your opponent controls, face-down.
  5. If your opponent activates a monster effect, Unicorn looks at their Extra Deck and banishes 1 monster face-down.

End board: Fenrir + Unicorn. Fenrir has already removed 1 of their cards for good, and you hold a second Fenrir.

  • Fenrir and Unicorn can't Special Summon themselves once you control a monster. Fenrir's search can't fetch Unicorn into a useful spot, so get Unicorn with Kashtiratheosis.
  • Kashtiratheosis's Xyz lock blocks all your Maliss Links. Use this line on a turn you aren't playing Maliss.

runick-typhoon.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Plan A — Fountain set-up (going first)

Runick is a control deck. Your Quick-Play Spells either disrupt your opponent or Summon a Runick Fusion from the Extra Deck, and each one banishes cards from the top of their Deck. Turn one sets up the engine: Inspector Boarder limits monster effects, Runick Fountain lets you cast Runick Quick-Plays from your hand on their turn, and Munin finds Runick Allure, which banishes their top card every time any Quick-Play is activated.

Starting hand: Inspector Boarder, Inspector Boarder, Terraforming, Runick Tip, Runick Flashing Fire · Normal Summon: Inspector Boarder

  1. Normal Summon Inspector Boarder while your field is empty (it can't be Summoned if you control a monster).
  2. Activate Terraforming: add Runick Fountain from your Deck.
  3. Activate Runick Fountain (Field Spell).
  4. Activate Runick Tip, Summon mode: Special Summon Munin the Runick Wings to the Extra Monster Zone. You will skip your next Battle Phase.
  5. Munin was Special Summoned from the Extra Deck: discard your second Inspector Boarder and add Runick Allure. Munin is a Fusion, so it opens 1 monster-effect slot under Inspector Boarder.
  6. Activate Runick Allure (Continuous Spell). Keep Runick Flashing Fire in your hand for your opponent's turn.

End board: Inspector Boarder + Munin + Fountain + Allure, with Flashing Fire in hand. Neither player can activate more monster effects per turn than there are monster card types (Fusion, Synchro, Xyz, Link…) on the field. If your opponent targets a Runick card or a Set card you control, Munin can banish itself to negate it. On their turn, Flashing Fire from your hand destroys a Special Summoned monster. Allure then banishes their top card, and Fountain recycles your used Quick-Plays.

  • Every Runick Quick-Play makes you skip your next Battle Phase, whichever mode you use.
  • Fountain's recycle-and-draw is once per turn and only targets Runick Quick-Plays already in your GY.
  • Inspector Boarder limits you too: with only Munin's type on the field, each player gets 1 monster effect per turn.
Plan B — Fonix on your opponent's turn

Radiant Typhoon Fonix Summons itself from your hand whenever any Quick-Play Spell is activated. Once it is on the field, the next Quick-Play activation lets it shuffle up to 2 of your opponent's cards into the Deck. Runick Fountain lets you activate Runick Quick-Plays from your hand on their turn, so you can disrupt, bring out a 3000 ATK monster and then clear 2 of their cards. Leave out Inspector Boarder for this plan: Fonix's effects are monster effects.

Starting hand: Radiant Typhoon Fonix, the Great Flame, Runick Freezing Curses, Runick Flashing Fire · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Have Runick Fountain face-up. On your opponent's turn, activate Runick Freezing Curses from your hand: negate 1 of their Effect Monsters and banish the top 3 cards of their Deck.
  2. A Quick-Play was activated: Special Summon Fonix from your hand.
  3. Fountain (once per turn, when you activate a Runick Quick-Play): put up to 3 Runick Quick-Plays already in your GY on the bottom of your Deck, then draw that many. The card you just activated isn't in the GY yet.
  4. Later that turn, activate Runick Flashing Fire: destroy 1 of their Special Summoned monsters and banish their top 2 cards.
  5. Fonix is on the field and a Quick-Play was activated: shuffle up to 2 of your opponent's cards into the Deck.

End board: Fonix (3000 ATK) is on your field. Their key monster is negated, another is destroyed, two more cards are shuffled away, and their Deck is 5+ cards thinner.

  • Each Fonix effect is once per turn: one Summon from hand and one shuffle (up to 2 cards). It is not 2 cards per Quick-Play.
  • You can only activate 1 of each Runick Quick-Play name per turn.
  • Super Starslayer TY-PHON on the field stops Fonix (3000 ATK) from using effects.
Plan C — TY-PHON off Fonix

Super Starslayer TY-PHON normally needs two Level 12s. It also has a shortcut: during the turn, or the turn after, your opponent Special Summoned 2 or more monsters from the Extra Deck, you can Xyz Summon it using just your highest-ATK monster. TY-PHON then stops both players activating effects of monsters with 3000+ ATK. It can also return a monster to the hand.

  2. In your Main Phase, Xyz Summon Super Starslayer TY-PHON - Sky Crisis using only Fonix (your highest ATK).

  4. Detach Fonix (its material) to return 1 monster on the field to the hand. A Fusion or Link sent back goes to the Extra Deck.

End board: TY-PHON (2900 ATK) with their best monster returned, and their 3000+ ATK monsters can't use effects.

  • The shortcut only works during the turn, or the turn after, they Special Summoned 2+ monsters from the Extra Deck.
  • TY-PHON's floodgate also stops your own 3000+ ATK monsters.

Line A — Mitsurugi first

This is the same Ritual line as Horus Mitsurugi, and it must come before Ryu-Ge War Zone. War Zone limits your Special Summons to Dragons, Dinosaurs, Sea Serpents and Wyrms for the rest of the turn, and every Mitsurugi monster is a Reptile. Prayers finds Murakumo, Mitsurugi Ritual Tributes Aramasa + Saji from your Deck, and Murakumo wipes your opponent's monsters when it arrives.

Starting hand: Mitsurugi Prayers, Mitsurugi Ritual · Normal Summon: Mitsurugi no Mikoto, Kusanagi

  1. Activate Mitsurugi Prayers without Tributing: add Ame no Murakumo no Mitsurugi from your Deck.
  2. Activate Mitsurugi Ritual (hand mode). Ritual Summon Murakumo by Tributing Aramasa + Saji (4 + 4) from your Deck.
  3. Murakumo was Special Summoned: destroy all monsters your opponent controls.
  4. Aramasa (Tributed) adds Futsu no Mitama. Saji (Tributed) adds Mitsurugi Mirror.
  5. Mitsurugi Mirror: Ritual Summon Futsu from your hand by Tributing Murakumo.
  6. Murakumo (Tributed) adds Kusanagi and Special Summons itself.
  7. Normal Summon Kusanagi: add Saji back from your GY.

End board: Murakumo + Futsu + Kusanagi. Murakumo makes your opponent discard or lose an effect, Futsu revives a Reptile when they Special Summon, and Kusanagi protects your other Reptiles.

  • Never activate Ryu-Ge War Zone before this line. Its lock stops every Reptile Special Summon, Ritual Summons included.
  • Each Mitsurugi monster's effects are once per turn by name.
Line B — War Zone into Mistva and the Realms

Sosei Ryu-Ge Mistva only Summons itself from the face-up Extra Deck, right after a monster on the field is destroyed. Ryu-Ge Rising puts it there. Ryu-Ge War Zone then Summons three Ryu-Ge monsters at once, and Anva destroys one of your own to trigger Mistva. Mistva destroys up to 2 of your cards and replaces them with Ryu-Ge Realm Continuous Spells. Each Realm gives your Level 10s a different Quick Effect.

Starting hand: Ryu-Ge Rising, Ryu-Ge War Zone · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Ryu-Ge Rising: add Sosei Ryu-Ge Mistva from your Deck, then put it from your hand face-up in your Extra Deck.
  2. Activate Ryu-Ge War Zone: take Kaiva (Dinosaur), Emva (Sea Serpent) and Hakva (Wyrm) from your Deck. Kaiva goes to your hand, Hakva is banished and Emva goes to the GY. Only Dragon, Dinosaur, Sea Serpent and Wyrm Special Summons from now on.
  3. War Zone (Mistva is face-up in your Extra Deck): Special Summon 3 Ryu-Ge with different Types. Anva comes from the Deck, Emva from the GY and Hakva from banishment.
  4. Anva was Special Summoned: target Emva and destroy it.
  5. A monster was destroyed while Mistva is in your Extra Deck: Tribute Hakva (a Level 10 Ryu-Ge on your field) to Special Summon Mistva. This counts as a Ritual Summon.
  6. Mistva: destroy 2 cards you control (War Zone and Anva). Place 2 Realms from your Deck: Wyrm Winds and Sea Spires.
  7. Anva was destroyed: place Ryu-Ge Realm - Dino Domains from your Deck face-up.
  8. 2 or more cards were destroyed this turn: Special Summon Kaiva from your hand (Quick Effect).

End board: Mistva (3500 + 300) + Kaiva + all three Realms. Mistva is a Ryu-Ge Pendulum, so it gains all three Realm effects, and Kaiva gains Dino Domains'. Dino Domains negates a monster effect from a monster with less ATK. Wyrm Winds makes a monster's ATK 0, and Sea Spires returns a card to the hand. Each Realm effect works by putting a Realm on the bottom of your Deck.

  • Mistva can only be Special Summoned by its own effect, once per turn. It Tributes from the field, so a Level 10 Ryu-Ge must be on your field.
  • You can control only 1 copy of each Realm.
  • Do Line A (Mitsurugi) before War Zone, never after.
Line C — Extend into Cosmic Blazar

Ringowurm is the deck's only Main Deck Tuner (Level 2). Normal Summon it after Line B, and a Level 10 Ryu-Ge + Ringowurm makes a Level 12 Dragon Synchro. Its GY effect then gives you a second Level 2 Tuner Token for a second Level 12. Crimson Dragon can swap itself for Cosmic Blazar Dragon, which banishes itself to negate a card, a Summon or an attack.

Starting hand: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples · Normal Summon: Ringowurm, the Dragon Guarding the Hundred Apples

  1. After Line B, Normal Summon Ringowurm (Level 2 Tuner).
  2. Synchro Summon Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon (Level 12) using Ringowurm + Kaiva (Level 10). It is a Dragon, so War Zone's lock allows it.
  3. You Synchro Summoned this turn: banish Ringowurm from your GY to Summon a Hundred Apples Token (Level 2, usable as a Tuner).
  4. Synchro Summon Crimson Dragon (Level 12) using the Token + Mistva (Level 10).
  5. Crimson Dragon (Quick Effect): target Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon, return Crimson Dragon to the Extra Deck and Summon Cosmic Blazar Dragon (Level 12). This counts as a Synchro Summon.

End board: Snake-Eyes Vengeance Dragon + Cosmic Blazar Dragon. Cosmic Blazar banishes itself until the End Phase to negate an activation, a Summon or an attack. Snake-Eyes turns a monster into a Continuous Spell during the Main Phase.

  • Using Mistva as material gives up the Realm effects. Only extend when the two Level 12s are worth more.
  • Crimson Dragon bringing out Cosmic Blazar follows a standing ruling. Confirm it with your judge.

Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Reichheart into Tri-Heart

Scareclaw monsters Special Summon themselves into a Main Monster Zone next to, or in the same column as, another Scareclaw. Light-Heart in the Extra Monster Zone opens the zone below it. It also searches the Field Spell Primitive Planet Reichphobia, which finds more Scareclaws. You end on Scareclaw Tri-Heart, which turns every face-up monster to Defense Position and ignores the effects of Defense Position monsters.

Starting hand: Scareclaw Reichheart, Scareclaw Acro · Normal Summon: Scareclaw Reichheart

  1. Normal Summon Reichheart in your Main Monster Zone. It adds Scareclaw Arrival (a Scareclaw Spell) from your Deck.
  2. Link Summon Scareclaw Light-Heart to the Extra Monster Zone using Reichheart.
  3. Light-Heart was Link Summoned in the Extra Monster Zone: add Primitive Planet Reichphobia.
  4. Activate Reichphobia: add Scareclaw Astra from your Deck.
  5. Activate Scareclaw Arrival: Special Summon Reichheart from your GY in Defense Position.
  6. Special Summon Scareclaw Acro from your hand in Light-Heart's column, then Scareclaw Astra next to a Scareclaw.
  7. Link Summon Scareclaw Tri-Heart (3 Effect Monsters) to the Extra Monster Zone using Light-Heart + Reichheart + Acro.
  8. Tri-Heart (in the Extra Monster Zone): Special Summon Acro from your GY and add Scareclaw Kashtira from your Deck. Then only Scareclaw Special Summons this turn.

End board: Tri-Heart (3000) + Astra + Acro + Reichphobia, with Scareclaw Kashtira in hand. Every face-up monster becomes Defense Position, including the ones your opponent Summons, and Tri-Heart ignores their activated effects. Reichphobia shrinks their monsters by 100 per Defense Position monster. In either Main Phase, Scareclaw Kashtira can Summon itself from your hand as a Quick Effect.

  • Reichheart's search is once per turn, so the copy revived by Arrival doesn't search again.
  • Light-Heart only searches if it is Link Summoned into the Extra Monster Zone, and only Main Monster Zone monsters can be its material.
  • Make Fusions, S:P Little Knight, Accesscode or Chaos Angel before Tri-Heart's revive effect, which locks you to Scareclaws.
Line B — Kashtira going first

Kashtira Fenrir Summons itself only while you control no monsters, so it is the first play of the turn. Its search should get Scareclaw Kashtira, which counts as both Scareclaw and Kashtira. Unicorn can't be Summoned once Fenrir is out. Scareclaw Kashtira stays in your hand and drops in as a Quick Effect on your opponent's Main Phase. Fenrir banishes 1 of their face-up cards face-down when they activate a monster effect.

Starting hand: Kashtira Fenrir · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. You control no monsters: Special Summon Kashtira Fenrir from your hand.
  2. Fenrir's Main Phase effect: add Scareclaw Kashtira from your Deck.
  3. Continue with Line A if you have a Scareclaw starter. Fenrir doesn't block Scareclaw Summons.
  4. Opponent's Main Phase (Quick Effect): Special Summon Scareclaw Kashtira from your hand, then banish 1 Kashtira or Scareclaw card from your hand or GY.
  5. When your opponent activates a monster effect, Fenrir banishes 1 of their face-up cards, face-down.

End board: Fenrir on the field and Scareclaw Kashtira as a surprise blocker. While your Kashtira or Scareclaw battles their monster, that monster's effects are negated.

  • Searching Kashtira Unicorn here is a trap: it can't be Summoned while Fenrir is on your field.
  • Kashtira Birth lets you Normal Summon Level 7s without Tributing if you need Unicorn on a crowded field.
Line C — Tri-Heart attack (going second)

Going second, the same board becomes an attack. Tri-Heart turns every monster to Defense Position, so their monsters can't hit back hard. Reichphobia destroys 1 of their cards once 3+ Defense Position monsters are on the field. Your Extra Monster Zone Scareclaw then attacks several times: Astra gives extra attacks, Acro adds ATK and Belone adds piercing damage. Super Polymerization first can remove a monster that would stop you.

Starting hand: Super Polymerization, Scareclaw Reichheart, Scareclaw Acro · Normal Summon: Scareclaw Reichheart

  1. Super Polymerization: discard 1 and fuse 2 of their monsters. For example, two DARK monsters make Starving Venom.
  2. Build Scareclaw Tri-Heart (Line A, steps 1–7). Tri-Heart turns all face-up monsters to Defense Position.
  3. 3+ Defense Position monsters are on the field: Reichphobia destroys 1 card your opponent controls.
  4. Tri-Heart: revive Acro from your GY and add Scareclaw Belone from your Deck. Special Summon Belone next to a Scareclaw.
  5. Battle: Tri-Heart attacks once per differently-named Defense Position Scareclaw (Astra), +300 ATK per Defense Position monster (Acro), with piercing damage (Belone).

End board: Tri-Heart attacks 3+ times with well over 3000 ATK, with piercing damage against Defense Position monsters.

  • Astra, Acro and Belone only boost Scareclaws in the Extra Monster Zone.
  • Reichphobia's destroy is once per turn and needs 3+ Defense Position monsters on the field (both sides count).

  • Super Polymerization ×3 with in-deck material pairs for every generic Fusion.

earthbound-resonator.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Line A — Soul Resonator into Crimson King and Scarred

Resonators are Fiend Tuners that build Red Dragon Archfiend Synchros. Soul Resonator finds Bone Archfiend, and Bone Archfiend sends Vision Resonator from your Deck to the GY, which searches Crimson Gaia. Soul + Bone make The Crimson King. Crimson King searches Power Vice Dragon, and Power Vice finds Darkness Resonator for a second Level 8, Scarred Dragon Archfiend. Earthbound Immortal Red Nova is the extra threat for your opponent's turn.

Starting hand: Soul Resonator, Super Polymerization · Normal Summon: Soul Resonator

  1. Normal Summon Soul Resonator: add Bone Archfiend. You can only Special Summon DARK Synchros from the Extra Deck this turn.
  2. Bone Archfiend: send Super Polymerization from your hand to the GY and Special Summon Bone Archfiend. Lock: DARK Dragon Synchros only.
  3. Bone Archfiend: send Vision Resonator (Fiend Tuner) from your Deck to the GY. Bone becomes Level 5.
  4. Vision Resonator was sent to the GY: add Crimson Gaia (it mentions Red Dragon Archfiend).
  5. Synchro Summon The Crimson King (Level 8) using Soul Resonator (3, Tuner) + Bone Archfiend (5, DARK).
  6. The Crimson King was Synchro Summoned: add Power Vice Dragon (it mentions Red Dragon Archfiend).
  7. All your monsters are DARK Synchros: Special Summon Power Vice Dragon. It adds Darkness Resonator.
  8. Reveal Red Dragon Archfiend in your Extra Deck to Special Summon Darkness Resonator. Lock: Synchros only.
  9. Synchro Summon Scarred Dragon Archfiend (Level 8) using Darkness Resonator (3, Tuner) + Power Vice Dragon (5, DARK).
  10. Activate Crimson Gaia. Its Main Phase effect adds Earthbound Immortal Red Nova from your Deck.

End board: The Crimson King + Scarred Dragon Archfiend + Crimson Gaia, with Earthbound Immortal Red Nova in hand. When they activate a monster effect, Crimson King banishes itself to Summon Red Dragon Archfiend at double ATK. In either Main Phase, Red Nova sends Scarred (named Red Dragon Archfiend) to Summon Red Nova Dragon.

  • Use Scarred, not Red Dragon Archfiend, as the second Level 8. Red Dragon Archfiend destroys your other monsters that didn't attack in your End Phase.
  • Scarred also bringing out Red Dragon Archfiend after Red Nova sends it is a timing ruling in your guide. Confirm it with a judge.
  • Almost every Resonator locks you to DARK (Dragon) Synchros for the turn, so Super Polymerization belongs on another turn.
Line B — Earthbound shortcut

Two copies of Earthbound Immortal Red Nova make a Level 12 boss with no Normal Summon. In either player's Main Phase, banish one Red Nova from your hand and send the other to the GY. Then Summon Red Nova Dragon from the Extra Deck, which counts as a Synchro Summon. Red Nova Dragon can't be destroyed by your opponent's effects and gets stronger for every Tuner in your GY.

Starting hand: Earthbound Immortal Red Nova, Earthbound Immortal Red Nova · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Main Phase (yours or theirs), Quick Effect: banish Earthbound Immortal Red Nova #1 from your hand.
  2. Its effect sends Red Nova #2 (an Earthbound Immortal) from your hand to the GY.
  3. Then Special Summon Red Nova Dragon from your Extra Deck. It counts as a Synchro Summon.
  4. Red Nova Dragon gains 500 ATK for each Tuner in your GY and can't be destroyed by your opponent's effects.
  5. Next turn, Red Nova #2 can use the same effect from the GY by sending a Red Dragon Archfiend (or Scarred) you control.

End board: Red Nova Dragon (3500+). When an opponent's monster attacks, it banishes itself to negate the attack, then returns in the End Phase.

  • Only 1 Earthbound Immortal can be on the field at a time.
  • Earthbound Immortal Red Nova's effect is once per turn by name.
Line C — Horus grind

The Horus cards are a second engine whose costs feed the Resonators. Imsety sends itself plus another card from your hand. Pick Vision Resonator, which then searches Crimson Gaia. Imsety finds King's Sarcophagus, Sarcophagus sends Hapi from your Deck to the GY, and both Horus Level 8s Summon themselves from the GY. This works even when your Resonator starter gets stopped.

Starting hand: Imsety, Glory of Horus, Vision Resonator, Bone Archfiend · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Imsety: send it + Vision Resonator from your hand to the GY. Add King's Sarcophagus, then draw 1.
  2. Vision Resonator was sent to the GY: add Crimson Gaia.
  3. Activate King's Sarcophagus. Send Bone Archfiend from your hand to the GY to send Hapi from your Deck to the GY.
  4. You control King's Sarcophagus: Special Summon Imsety and then Hapi from your GY.
  5. Activate Crimson Gaia. Bone Archfiend can later Summon itself from your GY by sending 1 card.

End board: Imsety + Hapi + King's Sarcophagus + Crimson Gaia, with Bone Archfiend ready in the GY.

  • King's Sarcophagus's send works up to 4 times per turn. Each discard can be a Resonator piece you want in the GY.
  • Imsety and Hapi each Summon themselves from the GY only once per turn.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell. You discard 1 card and Fusion Summon using monsters from EITHER field, and nobody can respond to it. Going second, you use it to turn two of your opponent's best monsters, or one of theirs and one of yours, into one Fusion Monster on your side. Pick the Fusion from what the two monsters have in common. Your own pairs: Bone Archfiend + Stone Sweeper (DARK Fiends) for Garura, and Soul Resonator (FIRE Fiend) + Bone Archfiend (DARK Fiend) for Flame Wingman.

Starting hand: Super Polymerization · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Super Polymerization by discarding 1 card. Neither player can respond to it.
  2. Both monsters share a Type and an Attribute but have different names → Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. If Garura later goes to the GY, you draw 1.
  3. Same Attribute but different Types → Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target it, or your monsters of its Attribute, with effects.
  4. Same Type but different Attributes → Favorite HERO Flame Wingman.
  5. Their two monsters leave the field as Fusion Material, so destruction protection doesn't save them. Then attack.

End board: Their two key monsters are gone and you have a Fusion Monster to attack with. You can also Set Super Polymerization and use it on your opponent's turn.

  • You choose the Fusion Monster. Check the Type and Attribute shown on each card before you activate it.
  • Fusions that must be Summoned another way ("cannot be Fusion Summoned" or contact Fusions) are not legal choices.
  • Almost every Resonator effect locks you to DARK Synchros. Use Super Polymerization on a turn without those locks, or on your opponent's turn.

  • Earthbound Immortal Red Nova gives a Normal-Summon-free Level 12 at Quick-Effect speed.
  • Horus engine adds a removal-punishing second plan and feeds the Resonator GY effects.
  • Strong hand-trap package for going second.

Mausoleum also puts Blue-Eyes White Dragon in the GY. Maiden places True Light, True Light revives Blue-Eyes, and Maiden comes back. Maiden + Blue-Eyes make Blue-Eyes Spirit Dragon, which stops GY effects and can become another Synchro on either player's turn.

Starting hand: Sage with Eyes of Blue · Normal Summon: Sage with Eyes of Blue

  1. Normal Summon Sage: add Maiden of White (a Level 1 LIGHT Tuner) from your Deck.
  2. Link Summon Spirit with Eyes of Blue using Sage. While you control it, you can only Special Summon Dragons.
  3. Spirit was Link Summoned: add Mausoleum of White. Activate it.
  4. Mausoleum gives an extra Normal Summon for a Level 1 LIGHT Tuner: Normal Summon Maiden of White.
  5. Mausoleum: target Spirit and send Blue-Eyes White Dragon from your Deck to the GY.
  6. Maiden: send itself from the field to the GY and place True Light face-up from your Deck.
  7. True Light: Special Summon Blue-Eyes White Dragon from your GY.
  8. You Special Summoned Blue-Eyes White Dragon, so Maiden of White Special Summons itself from the GY.
  9. Synchro Summon Blue-Eyes Spirit Dragon (Level 9) using Maiden (1, Tuner) + Blue-Eyes White Dragon (8).
  10. Tribute Spirit with Eyes of Blue: Special Summon Blue-Eyes White Dragon from your GY.

End board: Blue-Eyes Spirit Dragon + Blue-Eyes White Dragon + True Light. Spirit Dragon negates a GY effect once per turn, and neither player can Special Summon 2+ monsters at once. On either player's turn, Spirit Dragon can Tribute itself to Summon Lightstorm Dragon (destroys Spells/Traps) or Crimson Dragon. True Light stops your opponent targeting Blue-Eyes White Dragon.

  • Sage only searches when Normal Summoned.
  • If face-up True Light is sent from the Spell & Trap Zone to the GY, all your monsters are destroyed.
  • Spirit with Eyes of Blue only lets you Special Summon Dragons, which blocks S:P Little Knight and TY-PHON while it's on the field.
Line B — Primite opener

Primite Dragon Ether Beryl Sets Primite Lordly Lode, which searches Primite support and can Summon Blue-Eyes White Dragon from your Deck. The catch: after Lode's Summon effect, nobody's Special Summoned monsters can activate effects that turn, and that includes yours. Use Lode's Summon as your last play, and keep a Normal Monster on the field so Primite Drillbeam can be used for free.

Starting hand: Primite Dragon Ether Beryl · Normal Summon: Primite Dragon Ether Beryl

  1. Normal Summon Ether Beryl: Set Primite Lordly Lode from your Deck.
  2. Activate Lordly Lode: add Primite Drillbeam from your Deck.
  3. Last play of the turn: Lode declares Blue-Eyes White Dragon and Summons it from your Deck in Defense Position. Your Special Summoned monsters can't activate effects for the rest of the turn.
  4. Set Primite Drillbeam. While you control a Normal Monster, you can activate it without revealing a card.

End board: Ether Beryl + Blue-Eyes White Dragon + Lordly Lode + a Set Drillbeam. On your opponent's turn, Drillbeam negates and banishes 1 face-up card. Lode gives your Normal and Primite monsters 300 ATK per differently-named Normal Monster in your GY.

  • Lode's lock means Neo Kaiser Sea Horse, Spirit Dragon and other Special Summoned monsters can't use effects that turn. Do those plays before Lode's Summon.
  • Drillbeam re-Sets itself from your GY in your Main Phase while you control a Primite monster.
Line C — Tyrant Dragon (going second)

Wishes for Eyes of Blue finds a Tuner and Roar of the Blue-Eyed Dragons. Roar puts Blue-Eyes White Dragon on the field. Wishes then works again from the GY: it equips Neo Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon from your Extra Deck to that Blue-Eyes. A Blue-Eyes equipped with a Fusion can be Tributed to Summon Blue-Eyes Tyrant Dragon, which is unaffected by Traps and attacks every monster your opponent controls.

Starting hand: Wishes for Eyes of Blue, Effect Veiler · Normal Summon: Sage with Eyes of Blue

  1. Activate Wishes for Eyes of Blue by discarding 1 card. Add Sage with Eyes of Blue (Level 1 LIGHT Tuner) and Roar of the Blue-Eyed Dragons from your Deck.
  2. Roar: Special Summon Blue-Eyes White Dragon from your Deck in Defense Position. You can only Special Summon Dragons from the Extra Deck this turn.
  3. Banish Wishes from your GY: equip Neo Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon from your Extra Deck to Blue-Eyes White Dragon (+400 ATK).
  4. Tribute that Blue-Eyes White Dragon (equipped with a Fusion Monster) to Special Summon Blue-Eyes Tyrant Dragon from your Extra Deck.
  5. Normal Summon Sage: add Maiden of White for later.
  6. Battle: Tyrant Dragon (3400) attacks every monster your opponent controls once each. After a battle, it Sets a Trap from your GY.

End board: Blue-Eyes Tyrant Dragon clears their monsters, and Traps can't touch it.

Longyuan's Token + Longyuan makes Supreme Sovereign Chengying. While a Token is on the field you can only Special Summon Synchro Monsters from the Extra Deck.

Line B — Tenyi start

  1. You control no Effect Monsters: Special Summon Tenyi Spirit - Vishuda from your hand.
  2. Normal Summon Mo Ye. Reveal Suruya (a Wyrm) to Special Summon a Swordsoul Token.

  6. Suruya was material for a Wyrm Synchro: Special Summon Monk of the Tenyi from your Extra Deck and lose 1000 LP.

End board: Psychic End Punisher + Chixiao + Monk of the Tenyi. Your LP are now lower than your opponent's, so Psychic End Punisher is unaffected by their activated effects. Monk is a face-up non-Effect Monster, so in your next Main Phase you can banish Vishuda from the GY to return 1 of their cards to the hand.

  • Use the Token before you need Monk. While a Token is on the field you can only Special Summon Synchros, and Monk is a Link.
  • Monk Summoned by Suruya can't be used as Link Material.
Line C — Ecclesia (going second)

Going second, your opponent usually controls more monsters than you, so Incredible Ecclesia Summons herself for free. She Tributes herself as a Quick Effect to pull Mo Ye from your Deck. Mo Ye's Token makes Chixiao to negate a monster. With your Normal Summon still unused, Taia makes a Baxia, which shuffles 2 of their cards into the Deck. Clear their backrow first with Harpie's Feather Duster.

Starting hand: Harpie's Feather Duster, Incredible Ecclesia, the Virtuous, Swordsoul Emergence · Normal Summon: Swordsoul of Taia

  1. Activate Harpie's Feather Duster: destroy all Spells and Traps your opponent controls.
  2. Your opponent controls more monsters: Special Summon Incredible Ecclesia from your hand.
  3. Ecclesia (Quick Effect): Tribute her to Special Summon Swordsoul of Mo Ye from your Deck.
  4. Mo Ye was Special Summoned: reveal Swordsoul Emergence to Special Summon a Swordsoul Token.
  5. Synchro Summon Chixiao using the Token + Mo Ye. Mo Ye draws 1.
  6. Chixiao (Quick Effect): banish Mo Ye from your GY to negate 1 of their Effect Monsters.
  7. You control a Synchro: Swordsoul Emergence adds Swordsoul of Taia. Normal Summon Taia.
  8. Taia: banish Swordsoul Emergence from your GY to Special Summon a Swordsoul Token.
  9. Synchro Summon Baxia (Level 8) using the Token (WATER) + Taia (WIND). Two different Attributes, so shuffle up to 2 of their cards into the Deck.

End board: Chixiao (2800) + Baxia (2300) against a field with its best monster negated and 2 more cards shuffled away.

  • Ecclesia's End Phase return needs a Fusion Monster in your GY, and this deck has none.
  • Evenly Matched from hand needs you to control no cards. Use it at the end of a Battle Phase in which you played nothing.

Black Whirlwind finds Vata, and Vata sends itself plus Blackwings from your Deck to Summon Black-Winged Dragon. Black Feather Whirlwind and Shamal recycle your monsters. Sudri's Token becomes Boreastorm, and Boreastorm + Black-Winged Dragon make Black-Winged Assault Dragon.

Starting hand: Blackwing - Simoon the Poison Wind, Blackwing - Sudri the Phantom Glimmer, Blackwing - Shamal the Sandstorm · Normal Summon: Blackwing - Simoon the Poison Wind

  1. Shamal: send it from your hand to the GY to place Black Feather Whirlwind face-up from your Deck.
  2. You control no monsters. Simoon: banish Sudri from your hand, place Black Whirlwind from your Deck, then Normal Summon Simoon without Tributing. Only DARK Extra Deck monsters this turn.
  3. Black Whirlwind: a Blackwing was Normal Summoned, so add Vata (less ATK than Simoon's 1600).
  4. You control another Blackwing: Special Summon Vata from your hand.
  5. Vata: send Vata (2) + Sudri (4) + Harmattan (2) from your Deck to the GY (total 8) to Summon Black-Winged Dragon from your Extra Deck.
  6. Black Feather Whirlwind: you Summoned a DARK Synchro, so Special Summon the banished Sudri (less ATK than Black-Winged Dragon).
  7. Shamal in the GY: banish it to add Vata from your GY to your hand. Its 700 damage becomes a Black Feather Counter on Black-Winged Dragon instead.
  8. Sudri: Tribute Simoon to Summon a Phantom Glimmer Token (DARK Level 2 Tuner). The 700 damage becomes another counter.
  9. Synchro Summon Blackwing - Boreastorm (Level 6) using the Token (2, DARK Tuner) + Sudri (4). Boreastorm sends a Vata from your Deck to the GY and becomes Level 2.
  10. Synchro Summon Black-Winged Assault Dragon (Level 10) using Boreastorm (2, Tuner Synchro) + Black-Winged Dragon (8).

End board: Black-Winged Assault Dragon (3200) + Black Feather Whirlwind, with Vata in hand. Each time your opponent activates a monster effect, it gains a Black Feather Counter and deals 700. With 4+ counters, on their turn it can Tribute itself to destroy every card on the field.

  • In the End Phase, Simoon's Black Whirlwind goes to the GY and you take 1000.
  • Black Whirlwind only triggers on a Normal Summon, and only adds a Blackwing with less ATK.
  • Play Angelechy (LIGHT) before Simoon or Vata. Their DARK lock blocks every Angelechy Synchro.
Line B — Angelechy Problem

Angelechy Synchros sit face-up in your Spell & Trap Zone as Continuous Spells, and being placed there triggers their effects. Angelechy Problem Summons Enlisted and places Destrier, and Destrier searches Angelechy Opposition. Opposition gives your opponent an Angelechy monster and places Bastion, which places Shatranga. Destrier burns them, Bastion protects your Angelechy cards, and Shatranga limits their monster effects.

Starting hand: Angelechy Problem, Infinite Impermanence · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Angelechy Problem (Field Spell).
  2. Problem: discard Infinite Impermanence to Special Summon Angelechy Enlisted from your Extra Deck and place Angelechy Destrier as a Continuous Spell.
  3. Destrier was placed as a Continuous Spell: add Angelechy Opposition.
  4. Opposition: Special Summon your second Enlisted to your opponent's Main Monster Zone and place Angelechy Bastion in yours. Only LIGHT or DARK Synchros this turn.
  5. Bastion was placed: place Angelechy Shatranga as a Continuous Spell too.

End board: Your Enlisted, with Destrier + Bastion + Shatranga as Continuous Spells. Destrier deals 500 every time your opponent activates something, Bastion stops their effects destroying your other Angelechy cards, and Shatranga limits them to 5 monster effect activations per turn. Your Enlisted can banish an opponent's monster in an adjacent column.

  • Opposition's lock (LIGHT/DARK Synchros only) blocks Super Polymerization's Fusions, so use Super Poly first.
  • Problem's cost is a discarded Spell or Trap: spare Black Whirlwinds or Impermanence work.
Going second — Super Polymerization

Super Polymerization is a Quick-Play Spell. You discard 1 card and Fusion Summon using monsters from EITHER field, and nobody can respond to it. Going second, you use it to turn two of your opponent's best monsters, or one of theirs and one of yours, into one Fusion Monster on your side. Pick the Fusion from what the two monsters have in common. Your own pairs: any 2 different Blackwings (DARK Winged Beasts) for Garura, and a Blackwing + Black-Winged Dragon (DARK, different Types) for Mudragon.

Starting hand: Super Polymerization · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Activate Super Polymerization by discarding 1 card. Neither player can respond to it.
  2. Both monsters share a Type and an Attribute but have different names → Garura, Wings of Resonant Life. If Garura later goes to the GY, you draw 1.
  3. Same Attribute but different Types → Mudragon of the Swamp. Your opponent can't target it, or your monsters of its Attribute, with effects.
  4. Both are DARK monsters on the field (not Tokens) → Starving Venom Fusion Dragon.
  5. Same Type but different Attributes → Favorite HERO Flame Wingman.
  6. Their two monsters leave the field as Fusion Material, so destruction protection doesn't save them. Then attack.

End board: Their two key monsters are gone and you have a Fusion Monster to attack with. You can also Set Super Polymerization and use it on your opponent's turn.

  • You choose the Fusion Monster. Check the Type and Attribute shown on each card before you activate it.
  • Fusions that must be Summoned another way ("cannot be Fusion Summoned" or contact Fusions) are not legal choices.
  • Angelechy Opposition and Strategy Score lock you to Synchros. Use Super Polymerization before them.
blackwing-angelechy.str:
• Two independent engines (Blackwing, Angelechy).
  • Full Armor Master and Shatranga cap the opponent's monster effects.
  • Assault Dragon and Destrier punish activations with burn.

• Two mutually exclusive Extra Deck locks force careful sequencing.
  • Simoon and Problem have strict activation conditions (empty board, Spell/Trap discard).
  • No dedicated board breaker; Flame Wingman has no in-deck pair.

Line A — Eldam into Meghala and Fonix

The Radiant Typhoon monsters Summon themselves while your opponent controls no Spells/Traps, so they are free going first. Eldam finds Meghala. Meghala Summons a Radiant Typhoon from your Deck whenever a Radiant Typhoon Quick-Play or Mystical Space Typhoon is activated. Vision brings out Fonix that way and finds Mystical Space Typhoon. On your opponent's turn MST triggers Fonix, which shuffles 2 of their cards into the Deck.

Starting hand: Radiant Typhoon Eldam, Radiant Typhoon Vision · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Your opponent controls no Spells/Traps: Special Summon Eldam from your hand.
  2. Eldam was Special Summoned: add Radiant Typhoon Meghala.
  3. Special Summon Meghala from your hand the same way.
  4. Activate Radiant Typhoon Vision (Quick-Play) to add Mystical Space Typhoon from your Deck.
  5. A Radiant Typhoon Quick-Play was activated: Meghala Special Summons Fonix from your Deck. Only WIND monsters can be Special Summoned for the rest of the turn.
  6. Set Mystical Space Typhoon. A Quick-Play can only be activated from the hand on your own turn, so Set it for their turn.
  7. Opponent's turn: activate MST on their Spell/Trap. Fonix sees a Quick-Play and shuffles up to 2 of their cards into the Deck.

End board: Eldam + Meghala + Fonix (3000) with MST Set. On their turn, MST plus Fonix removes up to 3 of their cards.

  • Each Fonix effect is once per turn, so it shuffles up to 2 cards once, not 2 per Quick-Play.
  • Meghala's WIND-only lock blocks every Angelechy, Fusion and Link that turn. Do Line B first if you have both.
  • When MST destroys Vision, Chant or Manifestation, they Set themselves again, and MST revives Fonix or Varuroon from the GY.
Line B — Angelechy Problem

This uses the same Angelechy engine as Blackwing Angelechy. Problem Summons Enlisted and places Destrier, Destrier finds Opposition, and Opposition gives your opponent an Enlisted while placing Bastion. This Extra Deck has no Angelechy Shatranga, so Bastion's placement effect does nothing here. It still protects your other Angelechy cards. Spare Mystical Space Typhoons make good discards.

Starting hand: Terraforming, Mystical Space Typhoon · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Terraforming: add Angelechy Problem. Activate it.
  2. Problem: discard Mystical Space Typhoon to Special Summon Angelechy Enlisted and place Angelechy Destrier as a Continuous Spell.
  3. Destrier was placed: add Angelechy Opposition.
  4. Opposition: Special Summon your second Enlisted to your opponent's Main Monster Zone and place Angelechy Bastion in yours. Only LIGHT or DARK Synchros this turn.

End board: Your Enlisted, with Destrier + Bastion as Continuous Spells. Destrier deals 500 per opponent activation and Bastion protects your other Angelechy cards.

  • Do this before Meghala's WIND lock.
  • Opposition's lock blocks Super Polymerization, TY-PHON, S:P and Tri-Heart for the turn.
Line C — Going second with Fonix

Every Quick-Play Spell triggers Fonix, yours or your opponent's. The Fallen & The Virtuous destroys a card and Summons Fonix from your hand. Mystical Space Typhoon then destroys a Spell/Trap and triggers Fonix's shuffle. Fallen of Albaz finishes by fusing with 1 of their monsters.

Starting hand: The Fallen & The Virtuous, Radiant Typhoon Fonix, the Great Flame, Mystical Space Typhoon, Fallen of Albaz, Forbidden Droplet · Normal Summon: Fallen of Albaz

  1. The Fallen & The Virtuous: send Mirrorjade from your Extra Deck to the GY to destroy 1 face-up card. Fonix Summons itself from your hand (a Quick-Play was activated).
  2. Mystical Space Typhoon: destroy 1 of their Spells/Traps. Fonix is on the field, so it shuffles up to 2 of their cards into the Deck.
  3. Normal Summon Fallen of Albaz. Discard Forbidden Droplet to fuse Albaz with 1 of their monsters: Titaniklad (2500+ ATK) or Starving Venom (DARK).
  4. Battle with Fonix (3000) and your Fusion Monster.

End board: Up to 5 of their cards gone before you attack with Fonix plus a Fusion.

  • Nobody can respond to Super Polymerization, and that includes Fonix's Quick-Play triggers. Use a different Quick-Play to bring out Fonix.
  • Fonix's Summon and shuffle are each once per turn.

Line A — Gold Leo into Liger Dancer

Lunalight Liger Dancer, the deck's boss, is unaffected by every non-Lunalight card. It normally needs a long Fusion chain, but Kaleido Chick has a shortcut: send Leo Dancer from your Extra Deck to the GY and Kaleido counts as "Lunalight Leo Dancer" for a Fusion that turn. Gold Leo finds Silver Hound and discards it, Silver Hound pulls Kaleido from your Deck, and Polymerization fuses everything into Liger.

Starting hand: Lunalight Gold Leo, Polymerization, Lunalight Black Sheep · Normal Summon: Lunalight Gold Leo

  1. Normal Summon Gold Leo: add Lunalight Silver Hound, then discard Silver Hound.
  2. Silver Hound was sent to the GY by an effect: Special Summon Lunalight Kaleido Chick from your Deck. While Kaleido is face-up, only Lunalight monsters can come from your Extra Deck.
  3. Gold Leo (on the field): a Lunalight went to your GY, so add Silver Hound back to your hand.
  4. Kaleido Chick: send Lunalight Leo Dancer from your Extra Deck to the GY. Kaleido can be treated as "Lunalight Leo Dancer" for a Fusion this turn.
  5. Polymerization: Fusion Summon Lunalight Liger Dancer using Kaleido (as Leo Dancer) + Gold Leo + Silver Hound + Black Sheep from your hand.
  6. Kaleido was sent to the GY by an effect: add Polymerization back. Black Sheep was used as Fusion Material: add Gold Leo from your GY.

End board: Lunalight Liger Dancer (3800), with Polymerization and Gold Leo in hand. Liger is unaffected by non-Lunalight cards and attacks twice. As a Quick Effect it sends a Lunalight from your Extra Deck to destroy every monster your opponent Special Summoned.

  • Gold Leo's discard happens on resolution, so a discarded Silver Hound counts as "sent to the GY by a card effect".
  • Each Lunalight monster's effects are once per turn by name. Silver Hound returned to hand can't Summon from the Deck again this turn.
Line B — Fraktall start

Tri-Brigade Fraktall is a second way to get Silver Hound into the GY. Fraktall sends itself and Silver Hound to the GY, and Silver Hound Summons Gold Leo from your Deck. Gold Leo searches and discards Yellow Marten, Marten finds Lunalight Fusion, and Gold Leo returns Marten. Gold Leo + Marten make Perfume Dancer, and your Normal Summon is still unused.

Starting hand: Tri-Brigade Fraktall · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Fraktall: send it from your hand to the GY, then send Lunalight Silver Hound (a Level 3 Beast-Warrior) from your Deck to the GY.
  2. Silver Hound was sent by an effect: Special Summon Lunalight Gold Leo from your Deck. Only Lunalight Extra Deck monsters while Gold Leo is face-up.
  3. Gold Leo was Summoned: add Lunalight Yellow Marten, then discard Marten.
  4. Marten was sent by an effect: add Lunalight Fusion. Gold Leo returns Marten from your GY to your hand.
  5. Lunalight Fusion: Fusion Summon Lunalight Perfume Dancer using Gold Leo (field) + Marten (hand).
  6. Perfume Dancer was Fusion Summoned: add Luna Light Perfume.

End board: Perfume Dancer on the field, Luna Light Perfume in hand, and your Normal Summon free for a Gold Leo or Kaleido.

  • Fraktall's Link Summon effect is dead here: no Beast/Beast-Warrior/Winged Beast Link in this Extra Deck.
  • Lunalight Fusion is 1 per turn.

Line A — Starter into Gigantic Spright

Spright monsters are Level 2s that Special Summon themselves while you control a Level 2. Spright Starter pulls Jet from your Deck, and Jet searches another Spright Spell/Trap. Blue Summons itself and finds Red. Two Level 2s make the Rank 2 Gigantic Spright, which pulls Carrot from your Deck. Red and Carrot each negate an effect by Tributing another Level/Rank/Link 2 monster.

Starting hand: Spright Starter, Spright Blue · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Spright Starter: Special Summon Spright Jet from your Deck and lose 1300 LP. Only Level/Rank/Link 2 Special Summons for the rest of the turn.
  2. Jet was Special Summoned: add your second Spright Starter (for next turn).
  3. You control a Level 2: Special Summon Spright Blue from your hand. Blue adds Spright Red.
  4. You control a Level 2: Special Summon Spright Red from your hand.
  5. Xyz Summon Gigantic Spright (Rank 2) using Jet + Blue.
  6. Gigantic Spright: detach 1 material to Special Summon Spright Carrot (a Level 2) from your Deck.

End board: Gigantic Spright + Spright Red + Spright Carrot. When your opponent activates a monster effect, Red Tributes another Level/Rank/Link 2 to negate it. Tribute Gigantic, a Rank 2, and the monster is destroyed too. Carrot does the same against Spell/Trap effects.

  • Only 1 Spright Starter per turn. Pulling Carrot (1000) costs the least LP, but Jet searches.
  • Each Spright self-Summon is once per turn by name.
Line B — Dogmatika (going second)

Nadir Servant sends a monster from your Extra Deck to the GY and adds a Dogmatika monster with equal or lower ATK. Send Elder Entity N'tss (2500 ATK), which destroys a card when it hits the GY, and add Fleurdelis (2500). Your opponent has Extra Deck monsters, so Ecclesia and Fleurdelis both Summon themselves. Fleurdelis negates a monster when you control another Dogmatika.

Starting hand: Nadir Servant, Dogmatika Ecclesia, the Virtuous · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Nadir Servant: send Elder Entity N'tss from your Extra Deck to the GY and add Dogmatika Fleurdelis (2500 ATK or less). No Extra Deck Summons for you this turn.
  2. N'tss was sent to the GY: destroy 1 card on the field.
  3. A monster Special Summoned from the Extra Deck is on the field: Special Summon Dogmatika Ecclesia from your hand. She adds Dogmatika Punishment.
  4. Fleurdelis (Quick Effect): Special Summon it from your hand. You control another Dogmatika, so negate 1 face-up monster until the end of the turn.
  5. Battle: when a Dogmatika attacks, Fleurdelis gives all your Dogmatika monsters 500 ATK.

End board: Fleurdelis (3000 when attacking) + Ecclesia, with 1 card destroyed and their best monster negated. Set Punishment for their turn.

  • Nadir Servant, Ecclesia's search and Maximus all lock your Extra Deck. Do Spright plays before them.
  • Punishment locks your Extra Deck until the end of your next turn.
Line C — Evenly Matched into Sprights

Going second, Evenly Matched can be activated from your hand while you control no cards. At the end of your Battle Phase your opponent banishes face-down cards until they control as many as you. Skip your Main Phase 1, go to the Battle Phase with an empty field, and use it. Then build Line A in Main Phase 2 against a much smaller board.

Starting hand: Evenly Matched, Spright Starter, Spright Blue · Normal Summon: not needed

  1. Main Phase 1: play nothing, so you still control no cards. Enter the Battle Phase.
  2. End of the Battle Phase: activate Evenly Matched from your hand. Your opponent banishes face-down cards until they control as many as you.
  3. Main Phase 2: Spright Starter Summons Spright Jet from your Deck.
  4. Continue Line A: Blue → Red → Gigantic Spright → Carrot.

End board: Your opponent is down to 1 card, facing the Spright negate board.

  • Evenly Matched only works at the end of the Battle Phase, and from hand only if you control no cards.
  • Your opponent chooses which cards to keep.

gren-maju.lines:
Checked against official card text. Each step names the card it uses. Practice a line before you rely on it.

Plan A — Turn-one floodgates

This deck locks the game, then wins with one huge monster. Inspector Boarder limits monster effects, Necrovalley stops cards leaving the GY, and Macro Cosmos banishes anything sent to the GY. Every one of your cards that gets banished also makes Gren Maju Da Eiza bigger. Pot of Duality digs for the missing piece. It stops Special Summons that turn, but this plan only uses a Normal Summon.

Starting hand: Pot of Duality, Inspector Boarder, Necrovalley, Macro Cosmos, Solemn Judgment · Normal Summon: Inspector Boarder

  1. Pot of Duality: look at the top 3 cards and add 1. No Special Summons for you this turn.
  2. Normal Summon Inspector Boarder while you control no monsters.
  3. Activate Necrovalley (Field Spell). Cards in the GY can't be banished, and effects that move cards out of the GY are negated.
  4. Set Macro Cosmos (Continuous Trap) to flip on your opponent's turn.
  5. Set Solemn Judgment to stop their biggest Summon or Spell/Trap.

End board: Inspector Boarder + Necrovalley + Set Macro Cosmos and Solemn Judgment. Each player can activate only as many monster effects per turn as there are monster card types on the field. With Macro Cosmos up, anything sent to the GY is banished instead.

  • Your floodgates hit you too. Inspector Boarder also limits your hand traps, Albaz and Gizmek Orochi.
  • Don't Set Infinite Impermanence in a column with your face-up Continuous Spells. Its column lock negates them.
Plan B — Gren Maju burst

Gren Maju Da Eiza's ATK is 400 for each of your banished cards. Pot of Desires banishes 10 from your Deck, and Gizmek Orochi banishes 8 more to Summon itself. That makes Gren Maju 7200 ATK on a Normal Summon. Clockwork Night turns every monster into a Machine, so yours gain 500 and theirs lose 500. Clear the way with Raigeki first and this is lethal from 8000.

Starting hand: Raigeki, Pot of Desires, Gizmek Orochi, the Serpentron Sky Slasher, Gren Maju Da Eiza, Clockwork Night · Normal Summon: Gren Maju Da Eiza

  1. Raigeki: destroy all monsters your opponent controls.
  2. Pot of Desires: banish the top 10 cards of your Deck face-down and draw 2 (10 banished).
  3. Gizmek Orochi (Quick Effect): banish the top 8 cards of your Deck face-down to Special Summon it from your hand (18 banished).
  4. Normal Summon Gren Maju Da Eiza: 18 × 400 = 7200 ATK.
  5. Activate Clockwork Night: your monsters become Machines and gain 500. Gren Maju is 7700, Orochi 2950.
  6. Attack directly with both for 10,650 damage.

End board: A one-turn kill from a full 8000 LP.

  • Gizmek Orochi has a hard once per turn across both of its effects.
  • Don't use Pot of Prosperity on the same turn as Pot of Desires: Prosperity stops you drawing with card effects.
Plan C — Albaz steal-fuse

Fallen of Albaz fuses itself with one of your opponent's monsters when it is Normal Summoned. Pick the Fusion from what their monster is. Mirrorjade then banishes another monster, and Decisive Battle of Golgonda keeps your Fusion safe: send an Albaz Fusion from your Extra Deck instead of letting your card be destroyed.

Starting hand: Fallen of Albaz, Decisive Battle of Golgonda, Effect Veiler · Normal Summon: Fallen of Albaz

  1. Activate Decisive Battle of Golgonda (Continuous Spell).
  2. Normal Summon Fallen of Albaz. Discard Effect Veiler to fuse Albaz with their monster: Mirrorjade (an Extra Deck monster), Brigrand (Level 8+), Titaniklad (2500+ ATK) or Predaplant Dragostapelia (a Fusion).
  3. Mirrorjade (Quick Effect): send Titaniklad from your Extra Deck to the GY to banish 1 monster on the field.
  4. If your Mirrorjade would be destroyed, Golgonda sends Brigrand from your Extra Deck to the GY instead.

End board: Mirrorjade with Golgonda protection, and two of their monsters removed.

  • You run only 1 Albaz, so Titaniklad and Brigrand's End Phase Albaz search has nothing to find once Albaz is used.
  • Under Clockwork Night every monster is a Machine. That makes Mudragon and Alba-Lenatus impossible but Garura easy.

  • One Fallen of Albaz.
  • Deck-out risk (Desires ×2 + Orochi ×2 = 36 cards).
